name: HR & People
tagline: Headcount, attrition, tenure, pay, diversity and engagement from an employee list
description: Employee master and attrition extracts from HRIS and payroll tools (Darwinbox, Keka, greytHR, Zoho People, BambooHR, Workday, SAP SuccessFactors) and HR survey or analytics datasets.

fields.label: Salary / CTC
fields.description: Pay per employee in the file's own unit (usually annual CTC; some files hold monthly income).

subDomains.name: Employee master (HRIS)
subDomains.description: One row per employee, current and former, with hire and exit dates, status and pay.

subDomains.name: Attrition analysis snapshot
subDomains.description: One row per employee with a left/stayed flag and drivers such as tenure, overtime, ratings and satisfaction, without event dates.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.definition: Employees currently active, as of the file's snapshot.
kpis.formula: Distinct employees with an active status

variants.label: Distinct employees with an active status
Distinct employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Distinct employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as active.

pitfalls: Headcount is a point-in-time figure from the export; filtered by hire date it shows how many of those hires are still here, not historical headcount.

kpis.name: Attrition rate
kpis.definition: Share of everyone in the file who has left: a cumulative approximation of attrition.
kpis.formula: Exits ÷ employees in file (current staff + leavers)
pitfalls: Annual attrition divides one year's leavers by that year's average headcount. This cumulative ratio overstates it when the file holds many years of leavers and understates it when old leavers have been purged.

kpis.name: Voluntary attrition
kpis.definition: Share of employees who resigned of their own accord; terminations, layoffs and retirements are excluded.
pitfalls: Exit reasons are often recorded loosely ('personal reasons'); review the Value meanings mapping before trusting the split.

kpis.name: Average tenure
kpis.definition: Average years of service of current employees from the tenure column; without one, the average tenure of leavers from hire to exit, since a current employee's tenure needs an as-of date.
kpis.formula: Average tenure (years) of active employees, or average (exit date − hire date) ÷ 365.25 for leavers

variants.label: Tenure column, employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Tenure column, employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Tenure column, everyone
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers' tenure at exit is mixed in.

variants.label: Leavers: (exit date − hire date) ÷ 365.25
variants.caveat: No tenure column, and a current employee's tenure needs an as-of date, so this is the average tenure of leavers.

pitfalls: Survivorship: long-tenured stayers raise the average while early leavers drop out of it.

kpis.name: Average salary
kpis.definition: Average pay of current employees, in the salary column's unit.
kpis.formula: Σ salary ÷ count of active employees with a salary

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: Leavers' last salaries are included.

pitfalls: A few senior salaries pull the average up; the median is the better 'typical' pay.
Mixing annual and monthly figures, or currencies, makes the average meaningless.

kpis.name: Women in workforce
kpis.definition: Share of current employees who are women, among those with a recorded gender.
kpis.formula: Active female employees ÷ active employees with a gender

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers are included.

pitfalls: An overall share can hide that women are concentrated in junior levels; read it by job level too.

kpis.name: Employees in file
kpis.definition: Everyone in the file: current staff and leavers.

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No employee ID, so every row counts as one employee.

kpis.name: Exits
kpis.formula: Distinct employees with an exited status

variants.label: Distinct employees with an exited status
Distinct employees flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers are those flagged as having left.

variants.label: Distinct employees with an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: anyone with an exit date counts as a leaver, including people still serving notice.

kpis.name: Hires
kpis.definition: Employees whose hire date falls in the period.
kpis.formula: Distinct employees whose first hire date is on or after the period start
pitfalls: Rehired employees keep their original hire date in many systems, so they do not show as new hires.

kpis.name: Salary bill
kpis.definition: Sum of current employees' salaries, in the salary column's unit (usually annual CTC).

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: Leavers' salaries are included.

kpis.name: Average performance rating
kpis.definition: Mean performance rating of current employees, on the file's own scale.

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers' last ratings are included.

pitfalls: Ratings are often forced onto a curve and differ by manager; compare within a department or rating cycle.

kpis.name: Average engagement score
kpis.definition: Mean engagement or satisfaction score of current employees, on the survey's own scale.
kpis.formula: Average engagement score of active employees

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers' scores are included.

pitfalls: Survey non-response is not random: disengaged people answer less, so averages read high.

kpis.name: Training hours per employee
kpis.definition: Training hours delivered per employee with a training record.
kpis.formula: Σ training hours ÷ employees with a training value

variants.label: Σ hours ÷ distinct employees with a value
Σ hours ÷ rows with a value
variants.caveat: No employee ID, so every row counts as one employee.

kpis.name: Overtime share
kpis.definition: Share of employees flagged as working overtime.
kpis.formula: Employees with overtime ÷ employees with an overtime value

variants.label: Distinct employees with overtime ÷ with a value
Rows with overtime ÷ rows with a value
variants.caveat: No employee ID, so every row counts as one employee.

kpis.name: Involuntary attrition
kpis.definition: Share of employees who left through termination, layoff or the end of a contract.

kpis.name: Tenure at exit
kpis.definition: Average years from hire to exit for employees who left.
pitfalls: A low figure means people leave early: look at the tenure-at-exit histogram for a spike in the first year.

kpis.name: Median salary
kpis.definition: Middle salary of current employees: half earn more, half less.

variants.label: Employees not flagged as leavers
variants.caveat: No status column, so current employees are those not flagged as leavers.

variants.label: Employees without an exit date
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Everyone in the file
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers' last salaries are included.

kpis.name: Absence days per employee
kpis.definition: Days of absence per employee with an absence record.
kpis.formula: Σ absence days ÷ employees with an absence value

variants.label: Σ absence days ÷ distinct employees with a value
Employees without an exit date ÷ managers
variants.caveat: No status column: employees without an exit date count as current.

variants.label: Employees ÷ managers
variants.caveat: No status column, so leavers are included.

charts.title: Hires over time
charts.reason: Hires per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Exits over time
charts.reason: Leavers counted in the period of their exit date: discrete counts as columns from a zero baseline.

charts.title: Headcount by department
charts.reason: One count compared across named departments: sorted horizontal bars, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Headcount by gender
charts.reason: Part-to-whole with very few categories: a donut shows the workforce split at a glance.

charts.title: Average salary by job level
charts.reason: An average compared across levels: bars of the recomputed average pay per level; levels with under 20 people are hidden.

charts.title: Attrition by department
charts.reason: A rate compared across departments: attrition recomputed per department and sorted; departments with under 30 people are hidden as too small to judge.

charts.title: Attrition by job level
charts.reason: A rate across an ordered set of levels: bars of attrition recomputed per level; levels with under 30 people are hidden.

charts.title: Exit reasons
charts.reason: Leavers counted by reason and sorted, so the biggest fixable cause comes first.

charts.title: Attrition with and without overtime
charts.reason: Do people who work overtime leave more? Attrition recomputed for each overtime group, side by side.

charts.title: Engagement vs attrition by department
charts.reason: Two measures per department: a scatter with a trendline shows whether less engaged teams lose more people.

charts.title: Average salary by level and gender
charts.reason: Two categories and one measure: a level × gender grid compares pay like for like, which an overall gender average cannot (Simpson's paradox).

charts.title: Tenure at exit
charts.reason: How long leavers stayed: a histogram of tenure at exit reveals early-attrition spikes.

pitfalls: Attrition here is cumulative: leavers ÷ everyone in the file. Annual attrition divides a year's leavers by that year's average headcount, so treat this as an approximation.
Survivorship: employee masters often drop people who left long ago, so tenure, ratings and pay describe survivors and look better than reality.
Small groups swing wildly: attrition or pay for teams under about 30 people moves on one or two individuals, so rate charts hide them.
Simpson's paradox in pay and diversity: an overall gender pay gap can shrink, vanish or reverse within each job level when men and women are spread differently across levels.
Salary columns can mix annual and monthly figures or currencies across countries; confirm the unit before comparing averages.
People data is sensitive: IDs, ages, ratings and pay identify individuals, so share exports and screenshots with care.
